bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Government Forms Five-Member Panel to Address Examination Issues
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar Government Forms Five-Member Panel to Address Examination Issues Bihar Education Header News Published By - Hency Thacker August 24, 2026 Reading time - 2 min. Facebook X Copy URL WhatsApp The Bihar government has established a five-member expert committee aimed at recommending substantial reforms in the state’s examination framework. This initiative seeks to enhance the security, transparency, fairness, and effectiveness of examinations across various educational institutions and recruitment agencies. The notification regarding the committee’s formation was released by the General Administration Department on August 23. The committee’s mandate includes a comprehensive review of the examination procedures administered by state examination boards, commissions, and universities, as well as recruitment agencies. It will assess all aspects of the examination process—from candidate registration to question paper preparation, examination conduct, evaluation, result declaration, grievance resolution, and record keeping. The government has identified increasing complexity in the examination system, stemming from a growing number of candidates, the expansion of higher education options, intensified competition for government roles, and the adoption of digital technologies and artificial intelligence, necessitating these reforms. Focus on Preventing Malpractices A crucial area of scrutiny for the committee is the prevention of various forms of malpractice. This includes question paper leaks, impersonation, cheating, and tampering with answer sheets and examination results. The panel will also investigate security measures and protocols surrounding examination data to mitigate potential breaches.

bihar_raw_news.title: "Will review air connectivity, NH projects, preserving Bihar's heritage": JDU's Sanjay Jha on ...
bihar_raw_news.content: "Will review air connectivity, NH projects, preserving Bihar's heritage": JDU's Sanjay Jha on Parliamentary panel's visit ANI | Updated: Aug 24, 2026 09:55 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel Bihar ( Patna ) [India], August 24 (ANI): Chairperson of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Transport, Tourism and Culture and Janata Dal (United) leader Sanjay Jha said on Monday that the committee's visit to Bihar will focus on strengthening air and road connectivity, preserving the state's cultural heritage and developing tourism infrastructure. Speaking about the committee's three-day visit to Bihar, Jha said discussions will be held on the expansion of airports and air connectivity, including the international greenfield airport announced in the Union Budget, as well as national highway and road projects in the state. "There will be a complete discussion related to aviation. There will be a discussion on NH and road-related projects in Bihar, like Patna -Purnia, Gorakhpur-Siliguri and other projects like NH-27 , which are not in good condition," Jha told ANI. He said the committee will also review issues related to Bihar's art and cultural heritage, including the upkeep of museums, the Khuda Bakhsh Library and historical sites under the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI). "There will be a discussion on culture. We are going to the Bihar Museum and Khuda Bakhsh Library . There are many historical sites of ASI which are not well maintained, like Kumrahar. There will be a discussion on that," he said. The committee will travel to Gaya on Monday evening, where a meeting on tourism will be held on Tuesday. Jha said discussions will cover the development of major tourist destinations, including Bodh Gaya and Rajgir , as well as projects announced in the Union Budget. "Tourism is a very big sector for Bihar. We believe that if tourism succeeds, it becomes a very big sector for employment," Jha said. He said the committee's recommendations will be submitted to Parliament, following which the concerned departments will take further action. "When a committee comes, all the officers stay. So there is a detailed discussion. And then the timeline of other things is decided. The committee's report is submitted to Parliament. And then the department follows it up on the basis of this report," he said. Jha said the committee's visit was important for reviewing centrally funded projects and giving further momentum to development of transport connectivity, tourism and culture in Bihar. The committee will also visit Bihar Museum in Patna and later conduct on-site inspections of Bodh Gaya , Rajgir and Nalanda . (ANI)

bihar_raw_news.title: ET World Leaders Forum 2026: Bihar eyes 4x growth, 10 million jobs - The Economic Times
bihar_raw_news.content: Samrat Choudhary Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary emphasised that Bihar was scripting a development success story with an aggressive push to attract new investment in the state. Choudhary outlined the future trajectory of development, investment, industry, water management, employment, and infrastructure in the state while speaking to ET at The Economic Times World Leaders Forum. He coined a slogan ''Build Bihar, Believe in Bihar' to take the state through an industrial transformation in four years. "Bihar stands on the verge of transformation. We are guided by the principle of 'Build Bihar, Believe in Bihar', and restore the state back to the ancient glory where it used to be a centre of trade, education and good governance," Choudhary said. Also Read: Our reform express will move forward at even greater speed, says PM Modi "While Bihar lagged in development previously, essential infrastructure in fundamental areas-roads, electricity, and water-is now largely complete. The government's primary focus has shifted to industry, investment, and employment generation, backed by new policies designed to provide an enabling environment for domestic and global investors," he said. Live Events Talking about good governance, Choudhary emphasised the ' Sahyog Grievance Redressal Program ,' an initiative undertaken after he became the CM in April this year. Sahyog is a platform where a public complaint is monitored right from the time and it comes with a one-month deadline for resolution of the issue. "Out of 6,42,000 applications received so far, 96% have been resolved. A strict 30-day resolution deadline has been instituted, with provisions for disciplinary action and automatic suspension for officials demonstrating negligence or failing to meet deadlines," he added. The CM said the state has adopted a flexible approach in their industrial policy to accommodate investors prioritising the ease of doing business. "Tailormade policies have been introduced for Semiconductors and Global Capability Centres (GCC) in the current year. The government continues to facilitate land allocation, power access, and required amenities for industries. With a dense population, rapid technology adoption, and a substantial pool of trained human resources, Bihar offers investors both a vast consumer market and skilled labour," he said. Choudhary added that the power availability in the state has expanded from roughly 350 MW previously to over 10,000 MW, with the state providing approximately ₹23,000 crore in power subsidies to consumers. Currently, Bihar has four operational airports while 10 airport projects are underway. In road infrastructure there are six expressways in operation while several others are in the planning and construction phase. Choudhary specially highlighted that travel time between Patna Airport and Gaya has been reduced from four hours to approximately 1.5 hours. Water management remains central to the state's growth strategy. Samrat Choudhary laid out the work being done for effective utilisation of water available to the state through river water management. The CM said the total irrigated area has increased from 2.1 million hectares to 4.4 million hectares in recent years. national_raw_news.title: Telangana auto drivers call off indefinite strike after talks with Transport Minister Ponnam Prabhakar 2 hours ago 35
national_raw_news.content: Auto drivers in Telangana have called off their planned indefinite strike after successful talks with Transport Minister Ponnam Prabhakar. The strike was set to begin at midnight, but auto unions withdrew their protest after the government responded positively to their demands. Minister Ponnam Prabhakar thanked the auto unions for calling off the strike. He clarified that reports of RTC buying EV autos were false and mere propaganda. The government agreed to set up a Welfare Board for auto workers. A joint meeting between the Labour Department, Transport Department, and auto union representatives will be held on September 1 to finalise the rules for this board. Since auto fares haven’t been revised since 2012, the government agreed to raise fares after studying a proper report, and will issue an official order soon. The government also plans to launch its own app, similar to Ola and Uber. On the promised twelve-thousand-rupee benefit for auto drivers, the Minister said a decision will be taken after discussions with the Chief Minister, Deputy Chief Minister, and cabinet colleagues, considering the state’s financial situation. The government also announced financial support to convert old diesel and petrol autos into electric autos in Hyderabad’s core area, along with subsidies for buying new autos, to reduce pollution in the city. Transport Commissioner Ilambarthi, Additional Transport Commissioner Ramesh, and JTCs Chandrashekar Goud, Shiva Lingaiah, and Venkata Ramana were part of the talks with the auto unions.
